```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

# Load Packages
```{r}
library("tidyverse")
library("sf")
library("units")
library("vegan")
library("iNEXT")
```

# Load Data
```{r}
#Clear environment
rm(list = ls())

#Load in GBIF and site datasets
gbif_raw <- read_tsv("../data/0003154-260226173443078.csv") 
sites_raw <- read.csv("../data/DUG_sites.csv", na.strings = c("", " "))
```

# Clean and filter variables
```{r}
gbif <- gbif_raw %>%
  dplyr::select(decimalLatitude, decimalLongitude, coordinateUncertaintyInMeters, year, recordedBy,
                order, family, genus, species) %>%
  filter(year >= 2020)
```

# Spatial Geometry and Buffers
```{r}
# Convert raw coordinates to standard WGS84 spatial points
sf_data_wgs84  <- st_as_sf(gbif, coords = c("decimalLongitude", "decimalLatitude"), crs = 4326)
gardens.sf_wgs84 <- st_as_sf(sites_raw, coords = c("Long", "Lat"), crs = 4326)

# Transform coordinate systems to a metric projection (UTM or Albers) 
# so st_buffer uses true meters
# (Using EPSG:5070 - NAD83 Albers Conical Equal Area as an effective standard standard)
sf_data  <- st_transform(sf_data_wgs84, crs = 5070)
gardens.sf <- st_transform(gardens.sf_wgs84, crs = 5070)

# Create 1km buffer around garden points cleanly
buffer_distance <- set_units(1000, "m") 
gardens.buffer  <- st_buffer(gardens.sf, dist = buffer_distance)
```

# Spatial Join and Data Extraction
```{r}
# Assign observations to gardens based on spatial boundaries
sf_data <- st_join(sf_data, gardens.buffer["site_code"], join = st_within)

# Use st_drop_geometry() to completely scrub spatial vectors so data processing loops run fast and don't trip over metadata
gbif_data <- sf_data %>% 
  st_drop_geometry() %>% 
  filter(!is.na(site_code))
```

# Extract Biodiversity Metrics
```{r}
gbif_wide <- gbif_data %>%
  count(site_code, species) %>%
  filter(!is.na(species)) %>% # Protects against empty species classifications
  pivot_wider(names_from = site_code, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)

# Convert matrix column to actual data frame rownames so iNEXT reads site metadata correctly
gbif.iNEXTinput <- gbif_wide %>% 
  column_to_rownames(var = "species") %>% 
  as.data.frame()

# Run iNEXT to get richness and diversity estimates
gbif.iNEXT <- iNEXT(gbif.iNEXTinput, q = 0, datatype = "abundance")

# Extract richness indices
gbif_richness <- gbif.iNEXT$AsyEst[gbif.iNEXT$AsyEst$Diversity == "Species richness", ]
gbif_shannon  <- gbif.iNEXT$AsyEst[gbif.iNEXT$AsyEst$Diversity == "Shannon diversity", ]
gbif_simpson  <- gbif.iNEXT$AsyEst[gbif.iNEXT$AsyEst$Diversity == "Simpson diversity", ]

# Merge metrics cleanly back to site rows
sites_raw$gbif.rich    <- gbif_richness$Estimator[match(sites_raw$site_code, gbif_richness$Assemblage)]
sites_raw$gbif.shannon <- gbif_shannon$Estimator[match(sites_raw$site_code, gbif_shannon$Assemblage)]
sites_raw$gbif.simpson <- gbif_simpson$Estimator[match(sites_raw$site_code, gbif_simpson$Assemblage)]
```

## Prep family data code for NMDS
```{r}
# Push site_code directly to row IDs so vegan doesn't read it as count metrics
gbif_fam_wide <- gbif_data %>%
  count(site_code, family) %>%
  filter(!is.na(family)) %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = family, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>% 
  column_to_rownames(var = "site_code")
```


#Save Output Datasets
```{r}
#Site level data with landscape level rarefied GBIF floral data added 
write.csv(sites_raw,"../data/DUG_sites.csv", row.names = FALSE)

#Landscape Level iNat data from GBIF wide format
#Keep rownames TRUE to preserve site identifiers
write.csv(gbif_fam_wide,"../data/NMDS_datasets/gbif_fam_wide.csv", row.names =TRUE)
```
